title: I Built a Construction Sign for Messages That Need More Orange
author: Jason Lamb
excerpt: A browser generator for LED-style highway signs, with live previews, adjustable styling, and image or HTML export.

cover.alt: I Built a Construction Sign for Messages That Need More Orange cover image

content_html:
Some messages deserve more presence than a plain paragraph. Apparently, my solution was to build a miniature highway construction sign in the browser.

The Construction Sign Text Generator turns entered text into an LED-style message board. It uses a custom 5-by-7 dot-matrix renderer and supports one to four lines, with manual line breaks or automatic wrapping.

The controls make the appearance part of the fun. LED color, bulb size, spacing, glow, alignment, and the frame can all be adjusted. A live preview shows the result while the wording and layout change. It is a useful little exercise in making typography out of something other than ordinary font glyphs.

Export makes the preview reusable. The page can download a PNG image, copy self-contained embed code, or copy a complete standalone HTML document. Someone can use a static picture or keep the generated sign as a web element.

The project runs client-side and does not store entered text on a server. The files are ordinary HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, which fits the scale of the experiment.

What I like is the combination of a recognizable visual language and a very small task. A familiar road-sign style makes an ordinary message feel immediately different. The controls then turn that idea into something another person can customize.

It is not intended to manage an actual highway sign. It is a browser toy with a practical export button—and sometimes that is an entirely sufficient project brief.
